subject: MSA + DPA: transfer gap resolution & final tie-outs
messages:
From: Sophia Martin <sophia.martin@clearwell.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@clearwell.com
Date: 2027-05-09T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redlines: MSA + DPA - transfer annex & SCCs

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team attached redlines for the MSA and the Data Processing Addendum — the file is Clearwell_Redlines_MSA_DPA_20270509.docx (attached).

High level — three items blocking approval on our end that we'd like to confirm quickly:
1) SCCs / transfer annex: the current draft uses processor-to-processor language that our counsel says leaves ambiguity for onward transfers. We flagged the SCC annex and asked for a statement that clarifies subprocessor routing and that Redwood will route EU customer data to EU-only regions unless otherwise requested in writing.
2) KMS/key residency: we need either customer-managed keys (CMK) or a clear residency guarantee for keys used for encrypting EU data. The redline proposes a 90-day plan to provide proof of residency; our side wants it contractual.
3) Audit / evidence cadence: our security team expects 60 days notice for on-site/audit access; the redline currently retains 30 days. We marked that as an open exception.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the annex language in sections B and D of the DPA, or whether we need follow-up redlines? Also please confirm whether you can provide any SOC-2 type artifacts sooner (summary statements OK) — we can treat some items as conditional acceptance if evidence is provided before signature.

Timing: procurement is on a tight board deadline next week, so if we can close language this week that would be ideal.

Thanks,

Sophia Martin
Head of Legal Operations
Clearwell Health

Attachment: Clearwell_Redlines_MSA_DPA_20270509.docx (docx, 78 KB)
From: markus_klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Martin <sophia.martin@clearwell.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + DPA - transfer annex & SCCs

Sophia — thanks for the redlines and the clarity on the timing. I routed to legal and procurement (cc'd). Quick responses to the three items you called out:

1) SCCs / onward transfer: We can accept a tailored annex that specifies processor-to-processor flows, but need to keep operational fallback (region routing + onshore fallback) for edge cases where a customer explicitly requests a non-EU region. Proposed path: Redwood accepts the proposed annex language conditional on adding a short routing paragraph that we control via order form settings.

2) KMS residency: Redwood offers both customer-managed keys (via KMS integration) and Redwood-managed keys. For EU data we can commit to EU-resident keys for the life of the order form if that's required — but we need the MSA to allow for a technical implementation timeline (we suggest a 60-day implementation window post-signature). If Clearwell needs contractually guaranteed CMK, we will need procurement approval for the implementation SLA — can procurement confirm whether the board needs CMK or residency guarantees?

3) Audit notice: We can agree to increase to 45 days as a compromise if Clearwell provides written confirmation that any on-site requests will be scoped in advance. If Clearwell insists on 60 days we will escalate to the CS and legal leads for sign-off.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura, Ben: can you review the attached redlines and push back with exact legal language we want to propose? I've attached an internal marked-up PDF (marked-up_DPA_v2_internal.pdf) with inline comments.
- Sophia: if you can confirm whether CMK or residency is a hard requirement, we will prioritize that item.
- If we can converge today/tomorrow on those points we'll produce a tie-out doc for signature and loop procurement for DocuSign.

On timing, I appreciate the board deadline note — we'll treat this as high priority.

Best,

Markus Klein
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + DPA - transfer annex & SCCs (internal proposed text)

Markus / Sophia — reviewed. I've put proposed language below as clean snippets we can drop into the DPA; they are intentionally narrow to keep operational flexibility. Happy to discuss on a quick call.

PROPOSED SNIPPET 1 (Onward transfers / SCCs):
"Where Customer directs transfer of Personal Data to a non-EU Processing location, Redwood shall implement routing controls defined in the Order Form. Unless Customer expressly requests otherwise in writing, Redwood will process and store EU Customer Data within EU regions. Any onward transfer to non-EU Data Processors shall be subject to appropriate safeguards, including the EU SCCs (2021) or equivalent, and prior written notice to Customer."

PROPOSED SNIPPET 2 (Key residency / CMK):
"For Customer-designated EU Customer Data, Redwood will: (a) enable integration with Customer-managed key (CMK) solutions where available; or (b) if Customer elects Redwood-managed keys, Redwood shall ensure that the cryptographic key material used for encryption of EU Customer Data is stored within EU jurisdictions for the term of the Order Form. Implementation of customer-managed keys where requested shall be completed within sixty (60) days of execution, subject to reasonable cooperation."

PROPOSED SNIPPET 3 (Audit notice):
"Customer shall provide Redwood with no less than forty-five (45) days' prior written notice for any on-site audit requests. Requests shall include a narrowly scoped audit plan; redundant or duplicative requests may be declined or scheduled at Redwood's discretion."

Operational notes: we should add a short "Transfer Impact Addendum" clause referencing the 2021 SCCs and indicating a preferred annex (Annex II) for routing; that allows us to keep the MSA body lean and put jurisdiction specifics in an addendum that can be swapped out per-customer.

I've attached some redline snippets (redline_snippets.txt) and an internal commentary sheet. Ben: can you confirm whether procurement is OK with the 60-day CMK implementation window or whether we need to commit to a shorter SLA (I suspect procurement will push back).

If Sophia can confirm CMK vs residency preference we will produce a final tie-out and share via DocuSign link for signature.

Regards,

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + DPA - transfer annex & SCCs (updated redlines)

Laura / Markus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear snippets; very helpful. A few quick items from our side after internal counsel review:

- The SCCs snippet is acceptable provided the Transfer Impact Addendum is included in the executed DPA (we will need the annex as part of the signed package).
- On CMK: Clearwell's security team confirmed that EU-resident Redwood-managed keys are acceptable (we do not require CMK at signature) as long as there is a contractual residency guarantee for the key material.
- Audit notice: we can accept 45 days in the DPA.

Two outstanding asks:
1) Can Redwood confirm that routing controls will be surfaced in the Order Form UI and that a change to the routing setting requires written customer authorization (email is fine)?
2) Procurement notes an order form tie-out: we need the order form to list "EU region commit: yes" with the service region selector in the order form. That's procedural but critical for procurement sign-off.

I've attached our updated redline document (Clearwell_DPA_v3_20270511.docx) — it accepts the clauses above and includes two small edits: (a) explicit callout that routing changes require written authorization; (b) order form EU-region checkbox language.

If Redwood can confirm the two points above we are ready to sign and route DocuSign. If you prefer, we can accept the DocuSign packet that includes the MSA + DPA + Transfer Impact Addendum as a single envelope.

Best,

Sophia Martin
Head of Legal Operations
Clearwell Health
